intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the POGLUT1 gene (615618) on chromosome 3q13.33.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the POGLUT1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Study of affected and unaffected relatives confirmed correct segregation of the disease with the homozygous or compound heterozygous state for the POGLUT1 variants.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous and compound heterozygous POGLUT1 variants in patients with LGMD R21.

checks.claim: The POGLUT1 gene is located on chromosome 3q13.33.
checks.evidence_quote: Significantly, POGLUT1 is located within the 3q13.13‐q21.2 region of homozygosity in the affected siblings (Fig 3C).
checks.explanation: The paper places POGLUT1 in 3q13.13-q21.2. The specific band 3q13.33 is standard nomenclature that falls inside this region.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is a progressive myopathy affecting mainly the proximal muscles of the limbs (Servián-Morilla et al., 2016). Muscle biopsies show dystrophic changes, fewer satellite cells, and reduced glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan. Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) found that the disorder results from mutation in POGLUT1, a protein O-glucosyltransferase that adds O-glucose to EGF repeats found in Notch receptors. The mutation they identified greatly reduced the O-glucosyltransferase activity of POGLUT1 and was associated with reduced Notch signaling in patient muscle.

checks.claim: LGMDR21 is a progressive myopathy that mainly affects the proximal limb muscles.
checks.evidence_quote: the patients exhibited muscle weakness predominantly in the proximal lower limbs, with onset during the third decade. The disease course was progressive, leading to scapular winging and wheelchair confinement.
checks.explanation: Proximal, progressive weakness is stated directly.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in LGMDR21 show dystrophic changes.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscle biopsies from all four affected siblings revealed histological features ranging from very mild myopathic changes to classic dystrophic pathology (Fig 1A).
checks.explanation: The paper reports dystrophic pathology in the biopsies, although severity varied.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in LGMDR21 show fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Likewise, we found a decrease in PAX7 mRNA and fewer PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients compared with controls (Fig 5C and D).
checks.explanation: Patient muscle had fewer satellite (PAX7+) cells.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in LGMDR21 show reduced glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan.
checks.evidence_quote: Western blots showed a reduction in α‐dystroglycan glycosylation in patient muscle
checks.explanation: Reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation in muscle is stated.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) found that LGMDR21 results from mutation in POGLUT1.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings demonstrate that D233E mutation in POGLUT1 causes autosomal recessive limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy
checks.explanation: The paper states that the POGLUT1 mutation causes the disorder.

checks.claim: POGLUT1 is a protein O-glucosyltransferase that adds O-glucose to EGF repeats found in Notch receptors.
checks.evidence_quote: POGLUT1 is the sole enzyme that directly adds O‐glucose to a distinct serine residue of epidermal growth factor‐like (EGF) repeats containing a CXSX(P/A)C consensus sequence (Rana et al, 2011), many of which are found in Notch extracellular domains
checks.explanation: The enzyme's function is stated directly.

checks.claim: The POGLUT1 mutation identified by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) greatly reduced the O-glucosyltransferase activity of POGLUT1.
checks.evidence_quote: The D233E mutation dramatically reduces the O‐glucosyltransferase activity of POGLUT1, leading to impaired Notch signaling
checks.explanation: A dramatic reduction in activity is stated.

checks.claim: The POGLUT1 mutation identified by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) was associated with reduced Notch signaling in patient muscle.
checks.evidence_quote: Decreases in Notch1‐intracellular domain expression and in HES1 mRNA levels in skeletal muscle were detected compared with controls, which support that D233E affects Notch activity
checks.explanation: Reduced Notch signaling in patient muscle is reported.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) noted that this disorder has been named both limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2Z (LGMD2Z) and LGMD R21 POGLUT1-related.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) noted that LGMDR21 has been named limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2Z (LGMD2Z).
checks.evidence_quote: OMIM# 617232 named as LGMD2Z or LGMD R21 POGLUT1-related.
checks.explanation: The paper states the name LGMD2Z directly.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) noted that LGMDR21 has been named LGMD R21 POGLUT1-related.
checks.evidence_quote: OMIM# 617232 named as LGMD2Z or LGMD R21 POGLUT1-related.
checks.explanation: The paper states the name LGMD R21 POGLUT1-related directly.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) reported a consanguineous family with an autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy that began in adulthood, during the third decade. Affected members had progressive proximal muscle weakness. Muscle biopsies showed dystrophic features, reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation, and fewer satellite cells.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) reported a consanguineous family with autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: A consanguineous family from southern Spain comprises 17 individuals spanning three generations (Fig 1A). Four out of five siblings from generation II presented a phenotype consistent with a limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a consanguineous family with autosomal recessive LGMD.

checks.claim: In the consanguineous family reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016), the limb-girdle muscular dystrophy began in adulthood, during the third decade.
checks.evidence_quote: the patients exhibited muscle weakness predominantly in the proximal lower limbs, with onset during the third decade.
checks.explanation: Onset in the third decade is stated.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) had progressive proximal muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: the patients exhibited muscle weakness predominantly in the proximal lower limbs, with onset during the third decade. The disease course was progressive
checks.explanation: Progressive proximal weakness is stated.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies from affected members of the family reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) showed dystrophic features.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscle biopsies from all four affected siblings revealed histological features ranging from very mild myopathic changes to classic dystrophic pathology (Fig 1A).
checks.explanation: Dystrophic features were seen on biopsy.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies from affected members of the family reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) showed reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed a variable reduction in the glycosylated form of α‐dystroglycan at the sarcolemma in patients
checks.explanation: Reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation is stated.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies from affected members of the family reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) showed fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Likewise, we found a decrease in PAX7 mRNA and fewer PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients compared with controls (Fig 5C and D).
checks.explanation: Fewer satellite cells were found.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) reported additional patients with biallelic POGLUT1 mutations. All of them had limb-girdle muscle weakness, and age at onset varied, ranging from congenital to adult onset. On muscle imaging, fatty degeneration followed an 'inside-to-outside' pattern, with the inner region of each muscle in the anterior and posterior compartments of the thigh most affected. Muscle biopsies showed fewer satellite cells and alpha-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) reported additional patients with biallelic POGLUT1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we describe 15 patients from nine unrelated families from different countries carrying novel biallelic mutations in POGLUT1, broadening the presentation from congenital to adult onset.
checks.explanation: The paper reports additional patients with biallelic mutations.

checks.claim: All patients with biallelic POGLUT1 mutations reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) had limb-girdle muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients carrying novel mutations in POGLUT1 all displayed a clinical picture of limb-girdle muscle weakness.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Age at onset in the patients with biallelic POGLUT1 mutations reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) ranged from congenital to adult onset.
checks.evidence_quote: However, the age at onset was broadened from adult to congenital and infantile onset.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: On muscle imaging of the patients reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2020), fatty degeneration followed an 'inside-to-outside' pattern, with the inner region of each muscle in the anterior and posterior thigh compartments most affected.
checks.evidence_quote: The muscle imaging pattern resembled an “inside-to-outside” fatty degeneration because the most affected segment was the inner region of each muscle in the anterior and posterior compartment of the thigh.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies from the patients reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) showed fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: In accordance with the critical role of Notch signaling in regulating SC maintenance, we found a reduced number of PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients (Fig. 4b, c).
checks.explanation: Patients' muscle had fewer PAX7+ satellite cells.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies from the patients reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) showed alpha-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation.
checks.evidence_quote: Immunofluorescence staining with an antibody against glycosylated α-dystroglycan revealed a reduction of the glycosylated form of α-dystroglycan at the sarcolemma in all muscle biopsies
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of LGMDR21 in the family reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of LGMDR21 in the family reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: In a family with autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, we identified a missense mutation in POGLUT1
checks.explanation: Autosomal recessive inheritance is stated.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) studied affected members of a consanguineous family with LGMD and found a homozygous missense mutation in the POGLUT1 gene, asp233-to-glu (D233E). In functional studies, the mutant enzyme had reduced O-glucosyltransferase activity toward EGF repeats from Notch1. Patient muscle showed reduced Notch1 signaling and fewer satellite cells. Patient myoblasts showed abnormal myogenic differentiation. Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) suggested that a key disease mechanism is Notch-dependent loss of satellite cells.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) studied affected members of a consanguineous family with LGMD.
checks.evidence_quote: A consanguineous family from southern Spain comprises 17 individuals spanning three generations (Fig 1A).
checks.explanation: The study is of a consanguineous family.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) found a homozygous missense mutation, asp233-to-glu (D233E), in the POGLUT1 gene in affected members of a consanguineous LGMD family.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report a homozygous missense mutation (D233E) in the protein O‐glucosyltransferase 1 gene, POGLUT1, in four siblings with autosomal recessive limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy.
checks.explanation: The homozygous D233E mutation is stated.

checks.claim: In functional studies, the POGLUT1 D233E mutant enzyme had reduced O-glucosyltransferase activity toward EGF repeats from Notch1.
checks.evidence_quote: POGLUT1D233E also showed lower activity than wild type toward five different single EGF repeats from mouse Notch1 (Fig 4B)
checks.explanation: Reduced activity toward Notch1 EGF repeats is stated.

checks.claim: Muscle from patients with the homozygous POGLUT1 D233E mutation showed reduced Notch1 signaling.
checks.evidence_quote: Decreases in Notch1‐intracellular domain expression and in HES1 mRNA levels in skeletal muscle were detected compared with controls
checks.explanation: Reduced Notch1 signaling in patient muscle is reported.

checks.claim: Muscle from patients with the homozygous POGLUT1 D233E mutation showed fewer satellite cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Likewise, we found a decrease in PAX7 mRNA and fewer PAX7+ cells in the muscle of patients compared with controls (Fig 5C and D).
checks.explanation: Fewer satellite cells are reported.

checks.claim: Myoblasts from patients with the homozygous POGLUT1 D233E mutation showed abnormal myogenic differentiation.
checks.evidence_quote: Primary myoblasts from patients showed slow proliferation, facilitated differentiation, and a decreased pool of quiescent PAX7+ cells.
checks.explanation: Abnormal (facilitated) differentiation is reported.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) suggested that Notch-dependent loss of satellite cells is a key disease mechanism in POGLUT1-related LGMD.
checks.evidence_quote: These data suggest that a key pathomechanism for this novel form of muscular dystrophy is Notch-dependent loss of satellite cells.
checks.explanation: The authors state this conclusion directly.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) found homozygous or compound heterozygous POGLUT1 mutations in additional patients with LGMD. The disease segregated with the homozygous or compound heterozygous state in affected and unaffected relatives.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) found homozygous or compound heterozygous POGLUT1 mutations in additional patients with LGMD.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing data analysis identified nine missense and one nonsense recessive variants (homozygous or compound heterozygous) in the POGLUT1 gene, in 15 patients from nine independent families
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: In the families reported by Servián-Morilla et al. (2020), disease segregated with the homozygous or compound heterozygous POGLUT1 mutation state in affected and unaffected relatives.
checks.evidence_quote: Study of affected and unaffected relatives confirmed correct segregation of the disease with the homozygous or compound heterozygous state for the POGLUT1 variants.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) proposed that reduced O-glucosylation of Notch by mutant POGLUT1 lowers Notch signaling, which depletes the muscle satellite cell pool and impairs muscle regeneration. They also observed reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation in patient muscle.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) proposed that reduced O-glucosylation of Notch by mutant POGLUT1 lowers Notch signaling.
checks.evidence_quote: these observations suggest that the D233E mutation affects the self‐renewal of SC by reducing Notch signaling, likely due to defective O‐glucosylation.
checks.explanation: The proposed mechanism is stated.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) proposed that reduced Notch signaling due to mutant POGLUT1 depletes the muscle satellite cell pool and impairs muscle regeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: As a result, the investigated family shows a defect in Notch signaling with a significant depletion of satellite cells, resulting in defective muscle regeneration and ultimately leading to muscle dystrophy.
checks.explanation: Satellite cell depletion and impaired regeneration are stated.

checks.claim: Servián-Morilla et al. (2016) observed reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation in muscle from patients with POGLUT1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Western blots showed a reduction in α‐dystroglycan glycosylation in patient muscle
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

The mutation greatly reduced the O-glucosyltransferase activity of POGLUT1. Patient muscle showed reduced Notch signaling and fewer satellite cells.

checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report a homozygous missense mutation (D233E) in the protein O‐glucosyltransferase 1 gene, POGLUT1, in four siblings with autosomal recessive limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy.
checks.explanation: The homozygous D233E mutation in this consanguineous family is stated.
